extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of philosophy of science and physics (scientifically literate general audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Expository treatment of the concepts of persistence, transformation, and equivalence of physical forces, aimed at grounding scientific reasoning in epistemological postulates. Covers measurement, units, action–reaction, and empirical evidence for force transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative science requires units of measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative science implies measurement; and measurement implies a unit of measure. The units of linear extension (lengths of masses or spaces between marks) are the standards from which other measures are derived, and are assumed unchanged while temperature is unchanged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that all exact measurement ultimately depends on assumed standard units (e.g., the standard-measure preserved at Westminster). If these units were irregularly variable, many scientific verifications (astronomy, geodesy, trigonometrical surveys) would be impossible. Thus measurement presupposes constancy of certain physical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity of experimental inferences depends on constancy of units of force
rubrics_metrics.description: Inferences such as the indestructibility of matter (e.g., carbon mass remaining after combustion) are based on measurements given by scales and hence depend entirely upon the constancy of the units of force (gravitative force) used by those instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the gravitation of the standard weights varied, conclusions about matter's indestructibility would be invalid. Therefore experiments that aim to prove persistence of force tacitly assume the persistence/constancy of the units employed and cannot independently establish it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action and reaction equality entails persistence of force
rubrics_metrics.description: The equality of action and reaction is equivalent to asserting that Force is persistent; to assert equal and opposite action and reaction is to assert there cannot be an isolated force beginning and ending in nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denying equality of action and reaction would imply creation or annihilation of force. The text frames this as a conceptual necessity tied to the postulate that forces persist as antecedent causes of consequents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence of relations among forces (uniformity of law)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a given manifestation of force under the same form and conditions is preceded or succeeded by another manifestation, then under identical form and conditions the same antecedent will invariably relate to the same consequent; thus relations among forces persist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by examples (two equal bullets projected with equal forces, explosions with identical charges and barrels). Any claimed difference in outcomes with identical antecedents implies creation/annihilation of force. From this follows the uniformity of law: constant connexions among phenomena are deducible from the persistence of force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement cannot by itself prove persistence of force (ultimate postulate)
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be some principle which, as the basis of science, cannot be established by science itself; the Persistence of Force is such an ultimate truth which transcends demonstration and must be taken as a postulate underlying scientific inference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text argues that all reasoned conclusions rest on some postulate and that continued existence (persistence) of an unknowable cause underlies consciousness and scientific organization of experiences. Thus certain foundational truths are presupposed rather than proved by experiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forces undergo transformation and can be equivalent quantitatively
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical evidence (Meyer, Joule, Grove, Helmholtz, Faraday, etc.) shows that forces transform into one another (motion↔heat↔electricity↔magnetism↔light↔chemical action) and that definite amounts of one form yield definite amounts of others (quantitative correlations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides many concrete examples (motion producing heat, electricity from friction, heat generating motion in steam engines, electric currents generating magnetism, light producing chemical changes). Cites quantitative results like Joule's mechanical equivalent of heat (fall of 772 lbs. through one foot raises one pound of water one degree Fahrenheit) and Faraday's electrochemical measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical limits on establishing exact equivalence of forces
rubrics_metrics.description: Although forces are transformable and correlated quantitatively, it is often difficult to show exact equivalence because transformations generally produce multiple modes of force and proportions vary with conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author notes that transformations frequently yield several different resultant forces (e.g., momentum partly to gases, heat, sound), making precise accounting hard; nevertheless, certain experiments have yielded positive quantitative relations in special cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding force equivalence requires tracing transformations across sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: To comprehend that forces are unceasingly metamorphosed and nowhere increased or decreased, one must contemplate the various orders of changes studied across the concrete sciences and trace antecedents and consequents to see whence forces arise and what becomes of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text recommends examining a succession of phenomena (from celestial mechanics and nebular hypothesis to geological and chemical processes) to observe how motion, heat, light, and chemical action interrelate and conserve quantity through transformation.
